metadata.description: Version 1 answer of vibe app extras list: per declared ecosystem adapter of one installed version, which verbs the package declares, the author's recommended items with their enabled state, the list that would be installed, and what the adapter's list verb observes in that version. Every item string is opaque: vibe never parses, splits, quotes, escapes, validates or reorders one.
The installation key the listing is about.
The four verbs of an adapter; install is required of every one.
The recommendation's own token, which is also the id of the feature it is shorthand for.
The opaque item string, exactly as the author wrote it.
The synthesised feature is selected unless the user says otherwise.
The feature is in the chosen set this installation recorded, so the item is part of the list.
The user's own settings drop this recommendation by id, so its item is not in the list even when the feature is in the chosen set. A drop is honoured in every case, --no-extras included.
The adapter's opaque id, as the package wrote it.
The verbs this adapter declares, in verb order.
The author's recommended items in declaration order.

The final list that would be installed: the enabled author recommendations in declaration order, minus every one the user dropped, plus the user's own add items in their order, de-duplicated by exact string with the first occurrence winning. It answers the invocation's own --no-recommends / --no-extras posture, so a listing is an honest preview of the apply.
The user's own add list for this ecosystem, from [slot.<slot>.extras.<ecosystem>] of their config.toml, verbatim and in their order.
The recommendation ids the user declines there — ids, not items, because naming the author's row rather than re-typing their string is what keeps the two sides from drifting.

The list the adapter's install verb was last handed in this installation, from the inventory's own record. What was asked for, which a failed apply leaves standing and the live observation below may differ from.

What the adapter's list verb observed in this version. Absent when the adapter declares no list verb or the observation was not taken; an absent or empty answer file is an empty list and not an error.
Why the observation was not taken, when a declared list verb failed. The listing itself still answers.
What the listing reported and did not fail on.
